doc.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

title: First writing for big band at Berklee
summary: Her first large-ensemble piece at Berklee, and her lack of interest in big bands then.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I like that. Was that the first, at Berklee — let me rephrase — when was the first chance you had to write for a whole big band?

Probably about second year. They had a concert and the school asked me to write a chart for a concert. I had written a three movement piece. The second movement was with strings, the first movement was straight, the third movement had tympani and all of that whole thing. I’m not quite sure if it was good or not. Perhaps it wasn’t.
Was it your own composition too?
Well you jumped right into it, didn’t you?
Instead of just writing maybe a fairly straight ahead blues chart, you did your own thing.

Yeah, I think at that point I had ten years before that before I came to this country, I had ten years of my career in Japan. And I was doing pretty okay, I got to the point where I was playing probably faster than anybody and longer than anybody. That’s the whole thing. But a big band was something that I wasn’t quite interested in. I was interested in the individual players. I was mainly, and more than anything I was interested in my piano playing to be improved a little more. I sort of thought I could, and I always thought I could a little more improve, I could a little bit more improve. So that was because the school requested, that’s why I wrote that.
